name: diagram
description: Interactive Mermaid diagrams for chat agents, with two-way interaction between you, the agent and the diagram.

chatParticipants.name: diagram
chatParticipants.description: Draw, change and explain Mermaid diagrams

commands.name: new
commands.description: Start a new diagram instead of changing the current one

commands.name: explain
commands.description: Explain the current diagram or the selected nodes

disambiguation.description: The user wants to draw, visualize, update or explain a diagram, such as a flowchart, sequence diagram, class diagram, state machine, entity relationship diagram, architecture overview, mind map, timeline or Gantt chart.
examples: Draw a sequence diagram of the login flow
Visualize the class hierarchy in this file
Make a flowchart of this algorithm
Add error handling to the diagram

languageModelTools.name: diagram_render
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show a Mermaid diagram in an interactive panel
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Renders a Mermaid diagram in an interactive panel next to the chat, and reports whether it rendered or the syntax error if it did not. Use it whenever a diagram (flowchart, sequence, class, state, ER, mind map, timeline, Gantt, ...) helps explain code, architecture, data flow or a plan. In the panel the user can select nodes, edit the source and send follow-up requests about the selected nodes; call diagram_getState to see the current source and selection before changing a diagram. Always pass the complete diagram, not a diff. Avoid click directives, HTML and hard-coded colors.

source.description: The complete Mermaid diagram source, without a surrounding code fence.

title.description: A short title for the diagram, shown in the panel.

languageModelTools.name: diagram_getState
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read the diagram shown in the diagram panel, with your edits and selection
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the Mermaid source of the diagram currently shown in the interactive diagram panel, whether the user has edited it by hand, whether it fails to render, and which nodes the user has selected. Call it before changing an existing diagram, and when the user refers to 'this', 'these' or 'the selected' parts of the diagram.

scripts.compile: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.mjs
scripts.package: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.mjs --production
scripts.pretest: npm run compile && npm run compile-tests
